recertification.previous_factory_limitations: The colour-to-distance table is an arbitrary legend in the constructor (offsets list indexed by colour), not derived from the visible scene. It is therefore hard-coded via the palette rather than inferred from the demonstrations. Colours outside {2,3,4,8} (none occur in the generator's domain) are assigned offset 0, so they stay on the source edge; this follows the archived solver's fallback. The program assumes the background is palette[0]; the generator always uses 0 as background. Every generated scene has exactly one cell per row on the source line, so collisions cannot occur. If they did, cells would be painted in increasing offset order. No constructor defects or fixture contradictions were found: all three train pairs and the test pair agree with the uniform table. I have not run any tests.

uncertainty: Measurements are 1,000-sample statistics, not guarantees about every exported episode.

Strict shape contract: every original task has one input shape across demos and query. In 1,000 independent samples only 36-95 of ~370-550 shapes occurred >=4 times, so independently drawn pools will leave many queries without three distinct same-shape demonstrations (strict-sampling shortfalls; the contract must not be relaxed). Shape-conditioned context sampling is needed: all seven constructors accept a requested shape (tested). The root sampler's shortfall handling and rates were not inspected here and no fallback behaviour is claimed.
Proposal budgets come from measured worst-case acceptance (finite samples); exhaustion bounds are estimates except f45f5ca7 (analytic).
These families are not in prepare.py's native-repair list or admission.json (not edited here); they need root integration before entering the supplement.
